reproduction_target: Bulk RNA-seq transcriptomic comparison of porcine intestinal tissues (duodenum, jejunum, ileum, colon; 4 Large White pigs) and their derived 3D organoids: TAGADA v2.0.0 pipeline quantification (STAR mapping to Sscrofa 11.1.108 + StringTie), gene annotation via biomaRt/HCOP, TPM normalisation + filtering + MDS, cross-dataset comparison with GENE-SWitCH datasets and epithelial / innate-immune gene-set intersections, PCA developmental-trajectory projection, edgeR/limma-voom differential expression + variancePartition, and tmod CERNO feature-set enrichment. Wet-lab work (organoid derivation and culture, RNA isolation, library prep, NovaSeq sequencing) is out of computational-reproduction scope.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis from Methods sections 2.1-2.6. The whole TAGADA invocation (read QC, STAR mapping, StringTie assembly/quantification) is folded into a single step C1 because the paper cites it as one versioned pipeline call and gives no per-tool configuration. TPM normalisation, filtering and MDS are folded into C3 because they are described as one visualisation preprocessing block. The Fiji organoid-morphology image analysis (C9) is counted as a computational step even though its inputs are microscopy images, because it applies stated numeric thresholds to produce reported quantities. No study-specific code repository, script, notebook or pipeline config is provided anywhere in the paper; only the third-party TAGADA pipeline repository is cited.

steps.label: RNA-seq quantification with the TAGADA pipeline v2.0.0 (https://github.com/FAANG/analysis-TAGADA): reads mapped to pig genome reference version 11.1.108 with STAR, expression quantified with StringTie
Gene-name annotation using Biomart (v2.54.0) and the HCOP ortholog database (https://www.genenames.org/tools/hcop/, downloaded 03/17/2022)
TPM normalisation, filtering (genes >0.1 TPM in >=2 samples), log(TPM+0.5) transform and multidimensional scaling (MDS) in R ("The R Project for Statistical Computing", no version stated)

Expressed-gene comparison across TPM thresholds (gene expressed if TPM > threshold in >=3/4 replicates) and comparison with GENE-SWitCH liver/muscle/duodenum data (BioProject PRJEB58031); intersection with Wiarda et al. (2022) porcine ileum single-cell clusters 36 and 45 (epithelial, 1712/1789 genes retained) and with InnateDB v5.4 annotated genes (downloaded 2022/11/27, 1015/1226 retained)

PCA trajectory analysis on ileum samples plus GENE-SWitCH developmental stages (foetal F30, F70, newborn NB; BioProject PRJEB41970); stage centroids define a trajectory and tissue/organoid centroids are orthogonally projected onto it, repeated for all genes, EC genes and innate immune genes

Differential expression with edgeR Bioconductor package (v3.40.0): calcNormFactors normalisation, limma voom (v3.54.0) generalized linear model with gut segment and animal as fixed effects, likelihood ratio tests, FDR-adjusted p < 0.05, absolute logFC > 1 threshold
Variance-component analysis with the variancePartition package (v1.28.9), fitExtractVarPartModel over gut segment and animal factors

Feature Set Enrichment Analysis with the tmod R package (v0.50.13), CERNO method on ranked lists of annotated human orthologs by logFC (decreasing for up, increasing for down), GO:BP term sets from msigdbr_7.5.1, FDR < 0.05

Organoid morphology quantification by image analysis in Fiji from Olympus IX83 inverted-microscope images at day 7 of culture (particles > 2000 um^2 and circularity between 0.2 and 0.9 retained); area, circularity and count estimated

headline.static_readiness: 0/9 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: Under an inference-inclusive reading the ceiling is 1/9 RI and 8/9 NI-or-below. Only C1 (TAGADA v2.0.0) reaches RI, because it is the sole step backed by a public, exactly-versioned executable artifact; even there the study's own run configuration (sample sheet, profile, resource config) is absent. Every downstream analysis step (C2-C8) is code-absent: no repository, script, notebook or session record is provided, so exact R package pins (edgeR 3.40.0, limma 3.54.0, variancePartition 1.28.9, tmod 0.50.13, biomaRt 2.54.0, msigdbr 7.5.1) have no executable artifact to attach to and cannot lift those steps above NI. C9 (Fiji morphology) is X because the input microscopy images are not deposited and no macro is provided. This paper is not R-star-eligible via stage 2: there is no study code to verify.
headline.coverage: 9 computational steps assessed from Methods prose (sections 2.1-2.6); 4 wet-lab steps counted (W: organoid derivation/culture, RNA isolation, RNA quality/quantity assessment, library prep + NovaSeq 6000 sequencing) and excluded as OOS. The paper has an 'Availability of data and materials' statement (FAANG portal, PRJEB64165) but no code-availability statement.

gaps.where: All downstream analysis steps C2-C9 (annotation, normalisation/MDS, gene-set intersections, PCA trajectory projection, edgeR/limma DE, variancePartition, tmod FSEA, Fiji morphology)
gaps.missing: No study-specific code repository, R scripts, notebooks, Fiji macros, or pipeline run configuration is provided anywhere in the paper. There is no code-availability statement. Only the third-party TAGADA pipeline repository is cited.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit an analysis repository (GitHub + Zenodo DOI) containing the TAGADA run configuration and sample sheet, the R scripts for normalisation/filtering/MDS, the PCA-trajectory projection code, the edgeR/limma model code, the tmod/CERNO enrichment code, and the Fiji macro, with a sessionInfo() dump.

gaps.where: Software environment for all R analyses and for the TAGADA invocation
gaps.missing: No conda environment file, lockfile, renv.lock, container image or digest is claimed. The R version itself is never stated ('R (The R Project for Statistical Computing)'). Bioconductor release is not stated. STAR and StringTie versions appear only implicitly via the TAGADA v2.0.0 release; the TAGADA README declares container support (Docker >= 19.03.2 / Singularity >= 3.7.3) but the paper claims no image digest or profile.
gaps.how_to_close: State the R and Bioconductor versions, ship an renv.lock or conda-lock, and record the exact TAGADA execution profile and container image digest used.

gaps.missing: The raw Olympus IX83 microscopy images and the per-organoid measurement tables underlying area/circularity/count are not deposited; only the segmentation thresholds are stated.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the raw image set and the exported particle-measurement tables alongside the Fiji macro.

gaps.where: C2 HCOP ortholog table; C4 InnateDB gene set and Wiarda et al. epithelial cluster gene lists
gaps.missing: External resources are captured only by download date (HCOP downloaded 03/17/2022; InnateDB v5.4 downloaded 2022/11/27) or by reference to a published single-cell study (clusters 36 and 45). The concrete gene lists actually used (1712 EC genes, 1015 innate immune genes, the human-ortholog mapping used for CERNO) are not deposited as files.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the exact ortholog mapping table and the two derived gene-set files used, with their source URLs and retrieval dates, as supplementary machine-readable files.

gaps.where: C1 TAGADA parameters; C5 PCA trajectory projection
gaps.missing: TAGADA is invoked as 'Briefly, ... STAR ... StringTie' with no profile, no parameter overrides and no sample sheet. The PCA trajectory step describes centroid definition and orthogonal projection in prose only, with no statement of scaling/centering, component selection, or how the projection scalar is computed.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the pipeline run command and config file, and either the projection code or a fully specified mathematical description including preprocessing choices.

gaps.where: Wet-lab: organoid derivation from cryopreserved biopsies and culture/passaging (P3-P5), RNA isolation, RNA quality/quantity assessment (BioAnalyzer, Qubit, Nanodrop), library preparation and 100 bp paired-end NovaSeq 6000 sequencing
gaps.missing: Wet-lab generation steps are out of scope for computational reproduction (OOS); counted in W, not verdicted. Protocols are however published as FAANG SOPs, which is above-average practice.
